review_info.review_text: Loving the new restaurant Cielo in Carpinteria! Looks amazing, food was perfect and great prices! Service was five star and the pricing was 2 star but tasted 5 star!!!!! I'll definitely be back :))

CBG is out of business.  It is now Cielo.  There is a full bar, and the menu is a mix of flatbreads, burgers, tex-mex, assorted appetizers.  There is inside and outside seating.  Bar has 8 spaces so get there early.  I did not have a cocktail so I cannot comment on the bartenders mixing skills. Except I did observe the pop rocks martini...hmmm childhood memories ;)
I had the steak flatbread with onions and cheese.  Crust was paper thin and the steak was good but I was disappointed by a lack of seasoning.  The steak flatbread was overpriced for what you get.  The trip tip plate (tri tip, beans, rice and tortillas ) for 8 dollars looked like a better deal.

Today's agenda:  1. Head to Carpinteria  2. Try out the new Cielo's restaurant  3. Get food poisoning

Trust me this was NOT the intention.

My wife and I were so excited when Cielo's finally opened it's doors to the public after weeks of renovations after the take over of Cabo's.  Cabos' was one of our favorite go to spots for lunch and were hoping that Cielo's captured us as a regular the way it's predecessor did.

When we arrived we did notice the positives. The interior was definitely upgraded as the booths give it a more restaurant ambiance.  The bathrooms were nicely done and very clean.

We sat in the front patio overlooking Carpinteria Blvd and took our first look at the new menus.  First thing we notice were the prices were about 25% higher than Cabos which is cool if the food warranted that price.  It's the standard beach diner fare with a bit of a higher end take on it.  Sliders, burgers, chicken plates, salads, apps, etc.   Were were disappointed at the price of the drinks (house margs were $10) and NO pitchers of margs anymore!  That sucked as that was one of the highlights of Cabos.   

First time there we ordered the sliders.  Not bad but not great.  Heavy jalapeno overrode the beefy flavor of the meat.  They had a nice dessert menu and we ordered the carrot cake.  Not bad but the server had no idea where it was sourced from.  

The 2nd time we came we ordered the 1/4 chicken plate as that was our favorite dish at Cabo's.  Nightmare thru and thru.  Our plates arrived and we just looked at each other as the rice was in clumps.  Literally.  The rice and beans were cold to the touch and when we cut into the chicken it was RAW.   Dark pink RAW.  We called over the server and she apologized and took it back.  The same plates were returned with the same pieces of chicken grilled to a near burnt crisp (chefs revenge I'm guessing) and the rice and beans were still cold.  We called over the server to let her know and one of the owners came over to apologize.   We told her that we REALLY want to like this place as we LOVED Cabo's but the standards of the restaurant need to start with the standards in the kitchen and there is just NO care for the food here.  Even the cold beans had no flavor.  I texted my brother that we were here and his reply was "nice patio...terrible food".  

Anyway unfortunately unless there are some major changes in the kitchen I'm never coming back to Cielo's.   Post script the only reason I gave it 2 stars instead of 1 was the server was VERY nice and very helpful

review_info.review_text: Great Bartender, really knew how to make drinks.  Food kept changing.

review_info.review_text: Ok this is my dinning hall. I have it every week and the proteins are fresh. Like the sauce as well. Only cons: quite a long wait.

response: Rockfire Grill is a restaurant located in Goleta, CA that offers a variety of food options including chicken wings, sandwiches, breakfast and brunch, pizza, and burgers. The restaurant has outdoor seating and free Wi-Fi available. Customers can use street parking or lot parking, but valet parking is not available. The restaurant is rated highly with 4.5 out of 5 stars on Google. Customers have praised the food, service, and atmosphere at the restaurant. Many customers have also noted that the flatbread burgers are particularly popular and have described them as amazing. Some customers have also mentioned the chicken wings and seasoned fries as being delicious. Overall, Rockfire Grill seems to be a popular and well-regarded restaurant in the area.

source_info.name: Rockfire Grill
source_info.categories: Restaurants, Chicken Wings, Sandwiches, Breakfast & Brunch, Pizza, Burgers

review_info.review_text: Was a nice place good food and good service . Highly recommend. Lots of tvs for sports fans and overall good vibe

I really like Rockfire Grill. We were coming from LA  and stopped by there to grab something to eat. We got pizza, burger, and gyros. My daughter liked the burger. I liked all the food. Our pizza was  burnt at the bottom but they gladly renewed. Great customer service

My friend and I stopped in here to grab an outdoor dinner on a beautiful evening and we had a great experience! The patio has plenty of seating, service at the counter and efficient and our cashier gave great recommendations since we had never eaten here before. Loved the vibe, with the kind of surfy decor and a playlist that took me back to the Caribbean.

Let me start with the stars of the meal...the flatbread burger. Why aren't these a thing everywhere because they should be?! I ordered the East Bay BBQ and holy cow was it amazing. Meat was cooked to perfection, the house spread was something special, and the flatbread it came on was so good I basically have no words. My friend got the West Coast and she had the same reaction I did. We stuffed ourselves because it was so tasty. We also had chicken wings (with an absolutely delicious honey garlic sauce) and seasoned fries, both of which perfectly complemented the flatbread burgers.

I would order this whole meal again exactly the same way it was so good. Only wish we had one where I live (hint hint guys, open some more locations further down in SoCal). Already planning to take my boyfriend here next time we take a little day trip up to SB.

The Daily Grind is a local business located at 2912 De La Vina St in Santa Barbara, CA. It is a restaurant that offers a variety of options including sandwiches, breakfast & brunch, coffee & tea, food, and juice bars & smoothies. The business operates from 6:00 AM to 2:00 PM every day of the week. 

Customers have mentioned positive experiences with the coffee, bagels, pastries, and burritos at The Daily Grind. They appreciate the strong and tasteful coffee and the friendly and funny owner who works the cash register. However, there have also been some negative experiences reported. One customer found a bug in their salad, which was a disappointment. Another customer had their burritos given away and received poor service when the problem was not resolved. 

The business offers outdoor seating and free WiFi. It also allows takeout and is suitable for groups. The parking options include street parking and a parking lot. 

Overall, The Daily Grind has received an average rating of 3.5 stars from customers. While there have been some negative experiences, the positive aspects such as the coffee and friendly owner contribute to the overall appeal of the business.

response: Tri-County Produce Co is a locally owned market located in Santa Barbara, CA, offering a variety of fresh produce, specialty foods, coffee, tea, beer, wine, and spirits. According to customer reviews, the produce is fresh and of high quality, with some items not typically found in traditional grocery stores. The market also offers specialty breads, including Ethnic Bread, which can be special ordered. Customers appreciate the easy parking and friendly, helpful staff. Some customers have noted that the prices are higher than at larger supermarkets, but the quality and freshness make it worth the extra cost. The market also has a loyalty program that customers can join. One negative review mentioned issues with incorrect charging and poor customer service, but overall, the reviews suggest that Tri-County Produce Co is a great option for those looking for fresh, unique products and personalized service.

source_info.name: Tri-County Produce Co
source_info.categories: Coffee & Tea, Restaurants, Specialty Food, Beer, Wine & Spirits, Food, Health Markets, Grocery, Fruits & Veggies

review_info.review_text: Have recently rediscovered Tri County - and it's changed where I buy some of my fruits, vegetables, and breads.    The produce looks so different than most grocery stores - it seems to radiate freshness.    That freshness translates to flavor.    There are some breads available not in most stores, they even will special order breads you want from Ethnic Bread.    Parking is so easy, there's plenty of employees to help.  John Dixon and staff - thank you.   It's also nice to know one is shopping at a locally owned market - that's a plus.   Recommended highly.  My neighbors say the meats and fish are excellent too.  Don't forget to join their loyalty program also.

Check your receipts!  I was not only charged for 54 more green onions than I bought, I was also charged a $7.50 phone order fee (I didn't order by phone, I just walked in and shopped).  Once I noticed the charge I had to drive all the way back and the only compensation I was offered was the original $.89 green onion.  I used more gas than that driving all the way back.  If I had "accidentally" walked out with $56 worth of goods I didn't pay for i would not only have to return them all but I'd also be arrested.  Poor customer service.
I bought some fresh and organic vegetables, the price is more expensive than the supermarket, but the quality is very good.  I really like the grapefruit juice they squeezed by themselves.

response: Modern Times Academy of Recreational Sciences is a highly rated Beer Bar, Breakfast & Brunch, Vegan, Bars, Nightlife, and Restaurant located in Santa Barbara, CA. The business has a 4.5-star rating and offers a wide variety of beers, including IPAs and barrel-aged stouts, as well as a delicious menu that includes vegan options. The atmosphere is described as casual, trendy, and intimate, with outdoor seating and free WiFi available. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable about beers, and the business is known for its great selection of vegan food. Customers rave about the Munchwrap Supreme, which is similar to a Taco Bell favorite but plant-based, and the Ethereal Embrace, a unique and tasty drink. One customer noted that the girl working in the gift shop was particularly friendly and helpful, making the experience even more enjoyable. Overall, Modern Times Academy of Recreational Sciences is a must-visit spot for anyone looking for great beer, delicious food, and a welcoming atmosphere in Santa Barbara.

source_info.name: Modern Times Academy of Recreational Sciences
source_info.categories: Beer Bar, Breakfast & Brunch, Vegan, Bars, Nightlife, Restaurants

review_info.review_text: Such a great vibe there! I absolutely love Modern Times beer! I have been such a fan since my first Orderville and have followed deep into Monster's Park: Mexican hot chocolate edition! Mostly IPAs and barrel-aged stouts but everything is awesome. The vibe here is amazing and can't wait to come back, the staff is very friendly but...I must say, the girl working the gift shop in the brown plaid was seriously the sweetest! So friendly and so helpful. If everyone had employees like her, their business would be much more successful. She was very personable and relatable and also had great selections to offer. She even gave me good advice on a hoodie and also a "road-soda" to take with me! Her words were, "the ethereal embrace is fun to say and such a great treat at the end of a shift." She was absolutely right! What a treat to sip, on the way back to OC. This location needs to do what they can to keep her around because she is EXACTLY why people return to places like this. Not just because of the environment but because of the people who make the environment great! I unfortunately didn't catch her name but she is a keeper! Thank you again for such a great experience during my first time at a Modern Times location, you're what makes these places great, I thank you.

The Quick: INSANELY amazing food and awesome beer (lots of sours which we love). Get the munchwrap supreme ... Similar to a Tb favorite but plant based. Everyone who's been here has had trust issues after trying to vegan food... No one believes it's plant based. It's delicious, creative and sooo indulgent.  Enjoy yourself!
Best beers in town. Great vegan food and outdoor patio space as well. The staff is very knowledgeable about beers. The interior decor is really nice too.

response: Angel Oak is a well-regarded restaurant located at 8301 Hollister Ave, Santa Barbara, CA. Specialising in seafood, American (New) cuisine, and steakhouse-style dishes, the establishment holds a 4-star business rating. Angel Oak is open from 5 PM to 10 PM every day, and offers features such as free Wi-Fi, outdoor seating, and an upscale, classy, and romantic ambience. Customers have praised the staff's knowledge and friendliness, with a special mention to the server named Autumn. The menu features a variety of dishes including oysters, quail, halibut, and filet mignon, which have been particularly appreciated by the patrons. However, some customers have found the service to be slow, and one customer noted a lack of variety in the dessert offerings. The restaurant offers validated and valet parking but does not have a dedicated parking lot or street parking.

review_info.review_text:
Unfortunately, we came during the pre-fixed menu. There were no sides and no variety of appetizers. After reading the reviews of the food I was sad to see the menu look so bare and lonely. 
Our server was great, very friendly and the Sommelier was excellent. I chose the mushrooms, the lobster pasta and chocolate mousse. The mushrooms were hearty but the lobster pasta only had about 5 small pieces of lobster. My husband ordered the Ceasar salad, salmon and crème brûlée. He enjoyed his salad but the salmon filet was small.  With 3 (possibly small) 
 items per person, you may want to grab an appetizer in the lobby bar before you come. 
It also took forever to get each course. We were seated at 6:55pm and didn't leave until 9:25pm. My husband and son went back to the room while I waited at the table an additional 15 minutes for 2 cookies and a side of vanilla ice cream. I asked a manager who walked by to check on the dessert and to get me a copy of the itemized receipt. He seemed annoyed. Overall, maybe I'll return when the regular menu is back..

First off, I want to say all of the staff were amazing but we loved our server Autumn. She was so sweet and really knew the menu. We ordered everything she recommended. 

We got a bottle of wine to start, very crisp and light. Then for appetizers we ordered a dozen oysters which came in fresh from Baja, CA. I love that they provided a large amount of lemon, hot sauce and this amazing house made sauce. I could have eaten 100. One of the best selection of oysters we had. The quail and side salad was phenomenal. Just watch out for the little bones.

For dinner, I got the halibut which was so rich and tender I could barely scoop it up. It was very flavorful. Bae got the filet and potatoes which was cooked to perfection. We got a side of the cauliflower and it was the perfect side. 

We opted for the chocolate mousse cake since chocolate is my favorite but to be honest wouldn't recommend. I wish they would expand their dessert menu but overall great night sitting by the water!

Had a great time! Good service, drinks and food. Very knowledgeable. The filet mignon was amazing and finally found a place with a good bearnaise. Lots of tarragon and saffron on the menu. Would be 5 stars with a smidge lower price tag. The lighting was a little "shoe storey" but maybe because we were seated in the middle of the room. We also got wine recs starting close to $300. Apart from that a great experience.

response:
"Stella Mare's" is a highly-rated French restaurant located at 50 Los Patos Way, Santa Barbara, CA. It is known for serving a variety of American (Traditional), American (New), and French dishes. The restaurant operates from Tuesday to Saturday, between 17:00 and 21:00. The establishment offers free WiFi, outdoor seating, and allows reservations. It also provides parking in a lot, caters to group dining, and offers take-outs. 

Stella Mare's has a romantic and classy ambiance, which is appreciated by its customers. Patrons describe it as a beautiful place with a warm, upscale atmosphere, perfect for family dinners and celebrations. The restaurant's indoor greenhouse seating area is especially popular for its string lights and cozy fireplace. The service is rated excellent and the staff is noted for their accommodating nature. 

Customers particularly enjoy the restaurant's hearty bistro fare, including dishes like the lamb shank, Croque Madame, and Canard a L'orange. The complimentary warm sourdough bread and freshly baked mini blueberry muffins also receive high praise. The restaurant's selection of cocktails and wines are also appreciated by visitors.

review_info.review_text: Absolutely a beautiful French restaurant with history on the water. If you're dining at night, choose the greenhouse seating. They have string lights all over, making it a wonderful experience. It's still indoors, and heated so we did not feel cold even in December. The service was excellent and struck up a conversation with our waitress that also previously lived in the SF bay area. The food was excellent and pricing was so affordable. The lamb shank was near fall off the bone, and very tender and flavorful. Will return!

Such an adorable place, it reminds me of my grandmother's house with all the floral patterns, the decor is for sure very welcoming. 

We went there for a friend's birthday brunch. We were driving from LA to Santa Barbara for a day trip and were running late so we called them on our way and told them we would be 15 minutes late and they were very accommodating.

As soon as we arrived, we were welcomed by the host and taken to our table outside, it was a little cold so we asked if we could move inside and they had one table available which they set for us.

They brought us warm sourdough bread and freshly baked mini blueberry muffins, the muffins were delicious. 

I ordered the CROQUE MADAME which comes with a sunny-side-up egg, parts of the egg white were not cooked and I had to separate them, I am pretty sure I have seen it in many culinary shows that you should not serve the eggs with the white still raw. The rest of the sandwich was good. I was going to take a star away for this but we had such a pleasant experience that I decided not to.

first, we spent around 4.5 hours there and they still didn't try to throw us out! Second, the waiter was very sweet, he brought my friend a dessert with a little candle at the end that we appreciated a lot.

All in all, it was a pleasant experience and I will go back again but probably won't order the same food.

My father-in-law and his fiancée both had birthdays in November, so Matt B. and I took them out to dinner at Stella Mare's the night before Thanksgiving. It was a cold and dark out, even for our 6:15 reservation, and the restaurant was lovely, with a warm, cozily upscale atmosphere. We ate in a greenhouse room with high ceilings, tons of windows, and a fireplace. Service was good, and we enjoyed a pleasant meal. Even our 20-month-old had a swell time, though at some point, he insisted on walking around and hanging out by the fireplace. (He was mercifully well behaved, but did make eyes at the other diners.)

We started with a round of cocktails, which were pretty solid. I had a Smoky Margarita with smoky chili-infused tequila, house sweet and sour, and agave, finished with a spicy rim and a grilled lime wheel. Matt had L'Ancien, with Remy Martin cognac, Bulleit rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, Benedictine, and Angostura and Peychaud's bitters. We switched to wine for the rest of our meal. I forget what exactly, but some kind of nice red, no complaints there.

The food was classic hearty bistro fare without much trendy flourish, ideal for dinner with grandparents, plus there was a kids' menu for our toddler--we ordered him pasta with butter and parmesan, but I think he mostly ate bread from the complimentary basket. The rest of us started with the cheese plate and deviled eggs. The cheese plate came with three unidentified but tasty cheeses, accompanied by crostini, strawberry slices, golden raisins, and some kind of fruit jam. The deviled eggs, or oeufs mimosa au homard, were quite good, supple and topped with lobster tail slices, tobiko, pickled shallots, and dill, perched on a slab of toasted French baguette over a bed of arugula and olive oil.

For our entrées, Matt and I split the canard a l'orange and the filet mignon. The duck breast was cooked a touch more than we like, but it was otherwise decent, served with parsnip purée, roasted broccoli florets, charred red wine-braised shallots, orange gastrique, candied orange zest, and pea shoots. The steak was tender and satisfying. We got it with the cognac peppercorn sauce and it came with a heap of thin fries.

Since we were celebrating, we ordered dessert. I got the lemon cake, which was light and bright, with lemon curd filling, caramelized mascarpone cream, and vanilla sauce. I also tried a bit of my father-in-law's crêpe Suzette, which was great, with housemade crêpes, Grand Marnier, orange reduction, orange segments, and powdered sugar. Matt got some McConnell's vanilla bean ice cream, which he shared with our son--baby's first hesitant taste of ice cream.

I liked Stella Mare's and would be happy to come back. It feels like a place that will be around forever, and I look forward to more family dinners in that elegant greenhouse.

response: Wingman Rodeo - Milpas Street is a restaurant located at 730 N Milpas St, Santa Barbara, CA. Its offerings range from salads and sandwiches to chicken wings, catering to both vegetarians and non-vegetarians. The restaurant is open every day of the week from 4 pm, closing at 10 pm on weekdays and 10:30 pm on Fridays and Saturdays. The restaurant provides street parking, outdoor seating, free WiFi, and takeout services, but does not take reservations. The ambiance is described as trendy. Customer reviews are mixed, with the restaurant scoring an overall rating of 4 stars. Customers praised the variety of wings and sandwiches, with the bourbon wing being a particular favorite. However, some customers found the food to be overpriced and dry. One reviewer mentioned an issue with the outdoor heating system not being available on a cold day.

source_info.name: Wingman Rodeo - Milpas Street
source_info.categories: Salad, Restaurants, Vegetarian, Chicken Shop, Chicken Wings, Sandwiches, Nightlife

review_info.review_text: Tried 8 of their different wings. I'd say the bourbon one was my favorite. I wasn't a huge fan of the Thai peanut or the Parmesan wings, but the rest that I tried were decent like the chipotle lime, lemon pepper, and cali bbq. I ordered a raspberry coco mead but i guess that didn't have it in stock so the guy behind the counter brought out two different raspberry flavored beers for me to choose from. They also didn't have the chili watermelon boochcraft so we ended up choosing a different flavor. It was pretty cold out, and we asked if the overhead heater could be turned on and the response was that the heaters weren't ready, not sure what that meant, but we just ate our meal without the heater turned on.

Hidden gem on Milpas! Love coming to this place especially for happy hour. Great outdoor patio seating and nice ambiance. I haven't tried their wings but I really like the sandwiches and tenders.  Great flavor and good crunch to the chicken !

Sorry... how did person say that it was good?  Paid $41 for 7 chicken wing pieces, 1 honey Thai burrito and fries and 2- 8ozs. Cokes.  Wings were dry . Burrito was overfilled with dry white meat and little slaw.. off balanced. I have 1/2 left of burrito and will give to the homeless.

And last but not least, every time we've used this service the machine is always up to date with the latest hit songs, which makes the party that much more fun.  Highly recommended!

response:
Based on the provided structured data, here is an objective overview of Elsie's:

Elsie's is a popular local bar and restaurant located in Santa Barbara, California. With a cozy atmosphere and a unique blend of Grunge-style decor, Elsie's offers a welcoming environment for both locals and visitors. The establishment has a variety of amenities, including free Wi-Fi, outdoor seating, and a casual ambiance that makes it suitable for a wide range of customers.

The business hours are flexible, with Elsie's opening as early as 7:30 AM on weekdays and staying open until 2 AM on weekends. The bar and restaurant offer a variety of food and drink options, including coffee, tea, and alcoholic beverages. However, it is important to note that Elsie's does not accept reservations and has limited parking options.

The reviews for Elsie's are largely positive, with many customers praising the friendly service, cozy atmosphere, and unique decor. One reviewer noted that they had been coming to the establishment since moving to Santa Barbara and expressed their affection for the place. Another customer described the bar as having a "grunge-style garage" feel and appreciated the speakeasy-like atmosphere.

However, some reviewers have criticized the service at Elsie's, with one person describing it as hit or miss. Another reviewer noted that they had a poor experience with a surly bartender on their previous visit. Despite these issues, Elsie's has earned a 4-star rating based on customer reviews.

source_info.name: Elsie's
source_info.categories: Bars, Nightlife, Coffee & Tea, Food, Internet Cafes

review_info.review_text: I've been coming to this place since I moved to SB; such a friendly and warm environment, Love meeting new people there, the service is great and staff are lovely!

Bottom Line:  A great little bar



I CANNOT believe that I have never been to this place especially since I grew up in this town.

I love everything about this place; engine block coffee table, Cagiva gas tank in the rafters, lost of comfy places to sit, patio in the front and the back....the bar tender was super friendly and the people there were cool... and its got Pac Man!

Loved the Boont Amber too.  Check out this spot if you havent

Nice little hole-in-the-wall spot. 

If you're searching for Elsie's, you'll likely drive right past it. It's not really advertised from the street and I believe that this is intentional. While only a mere block or so from the best of downtown, its location is far enough off the beaten path that lends to the feeling of a speakeasy.

Elsie's is in a unique old building sectioned off into a few rooms. You'll find old couches (the kind you'll absolutely sink into), vibrant wall colors, and eclectic wall art. It's like a grunge-style garage from the '90s and truly brings me back to that era. There's also a great, large back patio along with a small front parklet area for Covid. There are two bathrooms which have seen far better days, but their dirtiness ties right into the old, endearing vibe of the place as a whole. 

Elsie's is beer and wine only - and cash only, although there's an ATM in front. I don't typically carry cash so must remember this fact when I come here. You'll find a very unique assortment of beers and I've tried a few good ones. I'd also tried their soju-based Bloody Mary once and it wasn't bad. 

Why three stars? Service can be a hit or a miss. I was here last night and the bartender was awesome. He was able to recommend some good beers for us and even provided a shot glass with a sample to try. Haven't always been this lucky, though. I was here about a year and a half ago (late 2019) and the female bartender working (dark hair, she's there often) was surly to the point that I'd decided not to come back in until just yesterday. I don't know if she's still here but I'd avoid at all costs if she is. Otherwise, a nice, comfortable local watering hole.

It operates between 10 am to 9 pm from Monday to Friday, opens at 10:30 am on Saturday, and 11 am on Sunday. La Salsa does not offer WiFi or parking facilities and does not accept reservations. However, it does offer outdoor seating and is good for groups. The restaurant has a casual ambiance and offers takeout options. With an average business rating of 3.5 stars, reviews for La Salsa are mixed. Despite the mixed reviews, La Salsa is recommended for its reasonable pricing and authenticity.

review_info.review_text: The salsa bar looks really fresh with reasonable pricing. I see that they're grilling the chicken on the spot and makes me look forward to my order

First off:  Don't eat here.

Second off:  Don't eat here. 

OK, so basically I just needed a quick lunch and I'm always down for a taco.  Hadn't been to a La Salsa in FOREVER, so this was a good plan (or so I thought).  I walked in and it was pretty busy, but by the time I placed my order it had cleared out.  I decided to get a Kids' Meal Quesadilla with black beans.

All in all things were fine with my meal; it was served hot so good so far.  (The only reason this review isn't 1 STAR is because their Mango Salsa.)  My soda tasted good, the chips were fine enough.  I began to eat my meal as I was sitting in one of the booths near the front door.

Another employee comes to the front door (near me) and starts spraying Windex and begins to clean the window.  I DO NOT want WINDEX in my food!  Then, she gets a broom and starts to sweep (no lie).  Then, gets out her mop and bucket and MOPS THE FLOOR.

This place is pretty small, so I could have given them a pass if she had mopped on the other side of the store, or oh, I DON'T KNOW WHEN THERE WERE NOT ANY CUSTOMERS around!?

Pretty gross.  Then, to top it off the employees started to BLAST the music so loud I didn't finish my basic queso.  

Nah, skip this place.

One of the FAVES to stop and eat when driving through Santa Barbara.  Why?

1.   It's fresh Mexican food made to order.
2.  Authentic style without grease
3.  Simple and easy to eat
4.  The salsa bar is small but diverse
5.  Great prices
6. Great location off the 101/154
7.  It's consistent!

So, definitely try it out.  Ignore the naysayers.
Try the Mexico City tacos!
Try the nachos.  They're HUGE!
Try the mango salsa too.

Enjoy!  You'll be back!!

Staying in Santa Barbara for the night, we decided to stop by here to pick up some grub to cook for dinner - albeit a little late (around 9-9:30).

The first thing I looked for was a tri tip.  They only had 3, and they were absolutely massive.  Something that you would buy for a huge party you would host.  But because there weren't any other options, we had to settle with 1/2 a cow.

review_info.review_text: I've been in here twice during the past 2 weeks & its always borderline dead. review_info.review_text: The only hazy on the strip! Much lower key and chill than the other breweries, but still has a couple of tvs to watch the game while listening to some Reggae!

A fire pit, live music, delicious beer, and sales that support an eco-friendly, sustainable cause? Fantastic! This was the line on loop in my head a few nights ago at Night Lizard. After several visits to this State Street brewery, I can easily say it's one of my tops. Staff are friendly, beers are tasty, and the vibe--whether sitting indoors or out--is neat. Gotta love all those hanging plants. 

Among beers tried are the Gnatcatcher IPA, Tiger Salamander Saison, and Monkeyflower Double White Ale. All are solid brews. I have yet to sample the food menu from Yona Redz, but look forward to it. 

There's usually room to sit on the outdoor patio, a Covid-safer option that offers great people-watching. I love holding a tulip glass of a tasty beverage, seeing folks passing by and eying the place. Thinking at them 'yes, you do want to stop here!' I smile a bit when someone does.
Trivia night is soooo cool. Best kombucha and seltzer. They say the beers are good too!

review_info.review_text: The only hazy on the strip! Much lower key and chill than the other breweries, but still has a couple of tvs to watch the game while listening to some Reggae!

A fire pit, live music, delicious beer, and sales that support an eco-friendly, sustainable cause? Fantastic! This was the line on loop in my head a few nights ago at Night Lizard. After several visits to this State Street brewery, I can easily say it's one of my tops. Staff are friendly, beers are tasty, and the vibe--whether sitting indoors or out--is neat. Gotta love all those hanging plants. 

Among beers tried are the Gnatcatcher IPA, Tiger Salamander Saison, and Monkeyflower Double White Ale. All are solid brews. I have yet to sample the food menu from Yona Redz, but look forward to it. 

There's usually room to sit on the outdoor patio, a Covid-safer option that offers great people-watching. I love holding a tulip glass of a tasty beverage, seeing folks passing by and eying the place. Thinking at them 'yes, you do want to stop here!' I smile a bit when someone does.
Trivia night is soooo cool. Best kombucha and seltzer. They say the beers are good too!

response: Sublime is a restaurant located at 901 N Milpas St, Santa Barbara, CA. It offers home services and American (New) cuisine but does not allow group reservations. The restaurant provides outdoor seating and takeout services. It has an average rating of 2.5 stars. A review from 2015 mentions that the food was good but pricey and suggests that the establishment should improve its branding. Another reviewer praises the restaurant's coffee and appreciates the evolving menu. A different review, however, criticizes the restaurant's service and ambiance, calling it sterile, and expresses dissatisfaction with the use of Miracle Whip in their dishes. The reviewer also mentions a lack of preparedness in terms of menu items.

review_info.review_text: Food was pretty good, although pretty pricy. I want a restaurant to succeed here, but where is the branding? The name Sublime comes with no info as to what kind of food is served. There is no identity established and no web presence. Even if the sign said, in big letters, "Sublime: Healthy California Cuisine" it would help a lot. To the owner: this is very basic business 101. You can't open a restaurant in 2015 without a website and a name that hints to the consumer what type of food you are serving!
Awesome coffee! Nice cafe in the area, looks like the menu is changing since they opened. Good to have a place to grab a beer and dinner on Milpas.

Sublime is new, okay we get it, but methinks a place should have their ish together just a smidge before opening their doors.  

Ambiance - sterile.  

Service - servers were nice, but slow and clueless.  They could not answer a single question about anything without having to run to the back to ask someone else.  

Food - decent enough.  I enjoyed the sage chicken.  My friend had the $40 steak dish (which I see is no longer on the menu) and the steak was juicy and delicious.  Congrats!  You made a yummy!  However, they use Miracle Whip in their deviled eggs.  Rewind....whuuuut??  Ew and moving on.  I looked forward to trying their tiramisu and after the server hyped it up, he told us it was not ready for the eating and wouldn't be until the next day.  Tiramisu tease!

A place that charges $40 for a dish should NEVER have Miracle Whip on the premises!!!  Where is your pride?!  Ohhh yeah, it's at the bottom of that jar of Miracle Whip.  It's miracle if they stay open, and it certainly won't be attributed to my returning patronage.

Dickey's Barbecue Pit is a local restaurant located at 7060 Hollister Ave, Ste 105 in Goleta, CA. It specializes in Southern-style barbecue cuisine. The restaurant is open from 11:00 AM to 9:00 PM every day of the week. The business offers takeout services but does not accept reservations. It does not have outdoor seating or WiFi available for customers. The atmosphere is described as casual.

Based on customer reviews, there are some negative experiences reported. One customer mentioned a poor online ordering experience, where they had to wait for a long time and were not informed about missing items in their order. The customer also mentioned that the staff did not offer any discounts or solutions to the problem. Another customer complained about the restaurant frequently running out of certain menu items, specifically ribs, and also mentioned issues with the ice cream machine.

Overall, the average rating for Dickey's Barbecue Pit is 2.5 stars. Despite being close to home for some customers, the negative experiences mentioned in the reviews may deter potential customers from visiting this establishment.

review_info.review_text:
I ordered online 45 minutes ago. I've been standing in line for ten minutes without being addressed. I finally get to the front, I'm told that my food isn't yet made AND he didn't bother to call and tell me that part of my order isn't available. He then says it will be another 20 minutes before my food is ready. When I mention that not waiting 20 minutes was the whole reason I ordered online 45 damn minutes ago, the guy working says the ownership is shit. That's probably true, but passing the blame isn't something I was ever allowed to do when I worked for The Man because it's not the customers fault, it's your job to offer a solution. I'd have gladly accepted an actual solution, but it was just this dude complaining that it's not HIS fault. Well dude, the owner probably does suck, but you're also bad at your job. I'm not sure the owner is the one who never once bothered to call about my order then acted like I was being unreasonable for suggesting that I should have been called. Did not offer a discount for the missing items OR the wait. Overheard him tell the next customer "Everything in this place is shit."

The food isn't even that good, I was getting it because it's close to home and I'm sick (thus the desire to not stand around for the rest of time immemorial). But now I won't even bother. I know this review makes me sound impolite but this is one of the first times I was ever annoyed with a place enough to come leave a review like this.

Edited to add: after I posted this, another customer came in who had ALREADY placed an online order (for which one has to pay in advance) and the worker refused to fulfill his order, told him to "call corporate" if he had an issue. Absolutely fucking ridiculous.

Awful!! Always out of something mainly ribs. Was the best when they had taco Tuesday but they stopped that. 

Every time I try to go they are out of most of their meats. Save yourself some time, NEVER go on a Sunday! 

If your lucky you might be able to enjoy the best thing they have. The FREE ice cream. That's if the machine is working 99% of the time it's not. 

Was very excited when this came in to town but ever sense it's been a disappointment. I would rather visit the Santa Maria or Ventura one. 

Hope they can turn things around too survive in this town. Good Luck.
How do you run out of ribs at a rib joint before 6:00 pm on a Sunday?Ask Dickey's because that what happened. No spinach, no sausages and no ribs.   Just wondering....

source_info.name: The Sportsman
source_info.categories: Bars, Nightlife, Dive Bars, Sports Bars, Lounges

review_info.review_text: This bar is awesome!  Didn't think much of it at first but our bartender Alice made our experience impeccable. Not only is she a great mixologist, she is down to earth and stole our hearts with her charm.  Thank you for making my birthday one of the most memorable ones.  Best bartender ever!

My husband Matt B. and I visited the Sportsman a couple weeks ago for a round of beers after dinner on State Street. We'd been to the Riviera the night before, which took over the Sportsman's old location, and were curious about this place, as it was apparently a Santa Barbara spot that had been around for ages. We stopped by around 10:30 on a Sunday night and it was pretty calm, with an unassuming dive bar atmosphere. There weren't a lot of people and we talked to the bartender for a while, a woman who's been with the bar for quite a long time.

We got a couple of draft beers--two IPAs on tap, I think Figueroa Mountain and Firestone--and played a couple rounds of pool. It's a good thing there weren't a lot of people around because we (and me especially) are absolutely dog shit terrible at pool. I was embarrassed that my own husband was there to witness my astounding lack of coordination. Like if someone wanted to blackmail me with the footage, I would probably be willing to pay. We should never do that in public.

Even so, it was fun, and the beer was good and refreshing. We enjoyed our visit to the Sportsman and would be happy to go back for more beer and maybe pool, as long as no one else is watching.

We love dive bars, especially when the bartender makes bloody Mary's from scratch! No premix crap! It was a Monday morning and the bloody mary really hit the spot. Very small place but clean. Locals spot, friendly people

review_info.review_text:
Is this place run by high school kids?

Took the time to make a reservation for New Year's Eve a month in advance as this restaurant has had special significance for my girlfriend and I.  Well dressed and looking forward to the prix fixe menu we walked in at 9pm to a half empty restaurant only to be sat on the patio.  Upset that after making the reservation so far in advance we were sat on the chilly patio.  I protested to the hostess only to be told that the empty tables were "reserved."  This is where I became enough of a pain in the ass to get the table we reserved.  It is worth noting that the restaurant sat half-empty for the entirety of our meal.

After being reseated inside we began the prix fixe dinner only to have food, obviously produced en masse and lacking attention to quality, thrown at us with such rapidity and voracity that we were almost unable to taste its run of the mill composition.  Almost.

Add to all of this an obnoxiously loud bartender and a waitstaff more interested in taking numerous cigarette breaks, and I'm very lucky to say that we managed to have an amazing and memorable evening DESPITE our experience at Elements.

But once we got home and compared our receipts/ bank accounts we realized that they added an ADDITIONAL gratuity once we left! Very sneaky. Only thing I'll be returning for is a price adjustment.

review_info.review_text:
The last time I went to Peabody's I had such a good time I just had to write a review.  Here's what happened:  I was sitting at the bar drinking a beer and eating some nachos when this gorgeous girl, Katie, and her friend walked in. They sat next to me and I noticed that Katie had the same phone as me, a crappy freebie phone they give you when you lose your iphone, and so I said, "Hey I like your crappy cell-phone, did you lose your iphone like me?"  As it turned out she had.  We swapped stories about how we had drunkenly lost our phones and after that we just kept talking.  She was making me laugh telling raunchy jokes and I was trying to impress her by weaving beach volleyball stories into the conversation.

The whole time the bartender kept our drinks flowing and made sure we were having a good time.  At one point when the conversation ran dry and I was about to pay my bill and go. Luckily I got the signal from the bartender, "stick around, this girl likes you." I'm hopelessly ignorant to the subtle signals of the opposite sex, and if I hadn't taken his advice I probably would have blown it.  We kept talking for a while and I finally asked her for her number.  Not only did she give me her number, but she walked with me to my car, gave me a kiss on the cheek, flashed me a smile, and made sure I was going to call her.

Needless to say, I did.  We met up a few days later for drinks and we had a great time.  We've been hanging out pretty steadily for a few weeks now and things are going really well.  I had to write a review and thank the guys at Peabody's for hooking me up.  I'm a regular at Peabody's now for sure.

My girlfriend and I were staying at the hotel behind this restaurant and decided to try it out after a long day of shopping and sight seeing. After reading some previous comments about service, we were a bit hesitant but decided to roll the dice. We were pleased to find that this place stayed open till midnight on weeknights. We arrived on a Thursday @ 10:30 p.m and were quickly greeted and told to sit anywhere we wanted. We sat next to a warm fire at the fireplace in the lounge but waited a very very long time for someone to take our order........we immediately started talking about the poor service stories we read earlier. After waiting for an eternity, I was forced to walk our order to the bartender (Warren) personally which he promptly took care of. We received our food and drinks in a timely manner and found the calamari and sliders to be hot , fresh, and very tasty. Again, we found ourselves searching for a server to refill our beers but to no avail and ended up walking to the bar for service. Although we found the service to be substandard as we read earlier.....the bartender (Warren) eventually personally came to our table and apologized for us being neglected and without hesitation offered to buy us a round of beers and shots of tequila. With that said, the service was as expected (we did get there @ 10:30 p.m. though) the food was very good, and Warren going above and beyond any other bartender ever has for us made our evening a very enjoyable experience. We highly recommend this restaurant and ask for Warren - he'll take great care of you.

      This place is totally avoidable....

Great simple sandwiches for really affordable prices.

This sams to go is great. Open when other delis are not. Food tastes fresh, service is a+

review_info.review_text:
Choppa Poke is in a plaza with a big parking lot. I came here on a Monday night and there was no wait time. 

I ordered a medium bowl which was VERY filling! They are extremely generous with the portion size and especially the protein scoops (which most poke places tend to skimp out on). The fish and all the toppings were fresh and overall it was really delicious. 

Choppa is more expensive when compared to other poke places; however, the price is justified by the fresh fish and generous portions! Will definitely come again(:

WORST experience ever. If you wish to be humiliated, do check them out.
 
Ordered their poke bowl in english and dined in with my husband. Thinking we could not understand mandarin, we later heard one of the female employees speaking to her colleagues pretty loudly about us and mentioning how disgusting we were as customers. In her exact words "Those two people who just came in, one male and female, having a bowl of poke bowl. Don't you think they are very disgusting?"  

I was extremely astonished to hear what she had said given that we did absolutely no wrong. And still find it puzzling why she would have said that. While we did not confront about the issue, we later walked over and spoke in mandarin, to let her know we understood mandarin too.  I guess it's just having a certain amount of basic respect and EQ to not badmouth about your customers so loudly. I hope the boss of this outlet is reading this and would educate your staff about customer service.

review_info.review_text:
Came here for breakfast since it was open decently early in the morning. The place is beautiful, but some issues with the bill and somewhat the food.

I had both the Crispy Yukon grilled potatoes, and the Lido's breakfast sandwich. The potatoes were delicious, and I found them to be more delicious than the sandwich. The potatoes also had a very generous serving.

The main issue I have, is the 20% service fee that is automatically added to your bill. It's not stated anywhere on the menu, or by the servers. Now I don't mind paying a 20% service fee if I was aware of it, but this restaurant does not notify you about it. Do not be fooled. Add tip on top of this, and you have a fee that's almost 40-50% of your meal. Would not come again.

New hours and the system as of Sept 5...now the restaurant is open for breakfast from 7am instead of 8.  Also, you can place your order with a server if you're dining in (instead of lining up at the bar counter).

The catch is...if you would like to dine outdoors, you'd have to wait till 8am when the pool opens.  Also, be aware it gets very busy between 9am and 10:30sh weekends as usual.

All servers are consistently good, friendly, and efficient!

Their lunch and dinner options are good as well.  I was going to have dinner @ Costa, but ended up eating (mussels) here after seeing someone else's meal.  ;)

The food is OK. The granola was not bad. The date shake was so so as well. It really got to me was it took forever for the waiter to come to the table. 

I'm top of that I can't stand companies that demand 20% gratuity regardless of service. I understand if it's a table of six or more etc. or even demanding 15 or 18 percent. But as someone who typically tips over 25% when I am demanded it really bothers me. If this has to do with fair wages then raise the prices of the items. Then you leave it up to the market to decide. But there's nothing posted anywhere that says a mandatory 20% tip. That's my other problem. If you're going to require that we need to disclose it on the front door.

review_info.review_text:
On Thursday night I went to this place after a concert. A few friends and I wanted a bite and a drink. We ordered with a young woman who quickly told us they did not accommodate gluten free customers, even if you wanted a taco or tostada without the bread. Fine. I'll work around that I understand. We waited 20 minutes for our food, granted there was only one guy in the kitchen. We finally got our tacos and were missing one chicken taco and our guacamole. We ask the chef for the rest of our order and he says they are closing the kitchen. I go to the woman and tell her that we didn't get all our food and she tells me I'm lying. I point to the plates on our table to show her we didn't. I ask for our money back and she declines. We end up getting into a fight about one chicken taco and guac. 

I have worked in restaurants before and I would never scold a customer over a $3 taco. I even offed to pay for it and she wouldn't let me. Really terrible customer service. The chef did make us some guac bc I think he felt bad that we were hungry and upset. By that point we had eaten what we were served and didn't have anything to put it on.

That being said the food we get was yummy. Too bad our experience ended on such a bad note.

We both got food poisoning here - that lasted a whole day. We narrowed it down to either the chips & salsa, the queso app, or the carnitas tacos since that's the only thing BOTH of us ate. The food seemed great, but it seems to be all about pushing the drinks for $$ and food safety was left to the sidelines.
Great food. WOnderful atmosphere. Great Happy hour two for one Margaritas. I love the decor too. Beautiful Bar. Amazing flan!

On Thursday night I went to this place after a concert. A few friends and I wanted a bite and a drink. We ordered with a young woman who quickly told us they did not accommodate gluten free customers, even if you wanted a taco or tostada without the bread. Fine. I'll work around that I understand. We waited 20 minutes for our food, granted there was only one guy in the kitchen. We finally got our tacos and were missing one chicken taco and our guacamole. We ask the chef for the rest of our order and he says they are closing the kitchen. I go to the woman and tell her that we didn't get all our food and she tells me I'm lying. I point to the plates on our table to show her we didn't. I ask for our money back and she declines. We end up getting into a fight about one chicken taco and guac. 

I have worked in restaurants before and I would never scold a customer over a $3 taco. I even offed to pay for it and she wouldn't let me. Really terrible customer service. The chef did make us some guac bc I think he felt bad that we were hungry and upset. By that point we had eaten what we were served and didn't have anything to put it on.

That being said the food we get was yummy. Too bad our experience ended on such a bad note.

We both got food poisoning here - that lasted a whole day. We narrowed it down to either the chips & salsa, the queso app, or the carnitas tacos since that's the only thing BOTH of us ate. The food seemed great, but it seems to be all about pushing the drinks for $$ and food safety was left to the sidelines.

review_info.review_text: Amazing service and amazing authentic Mexican food! A must try you won't be disappointed.

I came here for dinner with some friends. I have been to wanting to try this restaurant because I have heard good things about their food. I got two carnitas tacos, red steak enchiladas and a Michelada to go. Everything was tasty and flavorful! The steak enchiladas was wet with the red sauce and came with rice and beans. I don't usually eat beans, but their beans had a good taste and wasn't dry at all. The only reason why I didn't give them 5 stars is because they could have put more meat on the tacos and inside the enchiladas. Other than that everything was great and the michelada was definitely refreshing!

Most delicious bbq chicken in town... under radar spot for locals. On Saturdays only they grill some delicious marinated chicken. Order a half plate comes with hand made tortillas and chow down. Just melts in mouth so tasty, flavorful and fluffy. Their tacos are also really tasty during the week. Very nice staff, a real locals joint no tourists here. Maybe one of very best Mexican spots around Milpas which is saying a lot. Forget chicken ranch too much sodium aka heart attack 101. This is healthy and extremely tasty. Seasoning perfection.

review_info.review_text:
How lucky are you Montecito to have this restaurant in your backyard!  The tasting menu is such value for money and the food is outstanding!  Edward, a young amazing chef!  We are foodies and the food blew us away.  The Black Cod was perfection.  The portion sizes perfect.  The Wagyu Beef Tartar superb.  Could not fault a single thing if I tried.  Superb!   We need to support chefs and staff like these to elevate what is sorely lacking in SB. A vibrant food scene!  Ours is lackluster at best
Well done The Monarch!

Sorry to report that this restaurant is struggling. I loved their extensive menu at opening but now it's limited, expensive, only open for dinner Wed-Sun and the reason for the 2 stars is that the wood-fired oven isn't vented properly so it's incredibly smoky. We went there on a holiday weekend when everything else in the hood had an hour wait and it was nearly empty and we had to leave immediately since we couldn't handle the smoke. We have stopped by numerous times but encountered the same lingering haze that would require your clothes (and lungs) to be fumigated after. We were regular customers of the formerly owned restaurant and cozy bar (which is now a rarely used sushi 'by appointment' restaurant) so are saddened that this prime spot is being underutilized. Hopefully they will find their way.

Holy smokes. Monarch blew our minds - partly because we dropped in at 9:30 on a Wednesday night on our way up the coast (no expectations), but mostly because the flavor combinations were unexpected and meticulously crafted. Surprise, surprise - our impromptu road trip dinner turned out to be a Michelin-worthy artistic experience! Imaginative, delectable, layers of flavor, unique, pure magic. The kind of food you don't want to destroy with a utensil, but when you do, you just have to close your eyes and let the sensations wash over you. It's that good.

The following night (Thursday) beckoned to us with the promise of dinner at the Post Ranch Inn (the renowned Sierra Mar restaurant) where we planned to celebrate my husband's 40th birthday. Well no offense to Post Ranch, but Monarch outshined it in terms of culinary art. (Post Ranch was spectacular for the views, architecture, and experience - and the food was also very good - but at twice the price and half the flavor, held no candle to Monarch.)

If Monarch were in our area of Los Angeles, it would cost double the price and be booked out months in advance. In response to those reviewers complaining about price point, portions, and "fanciness," please don't review all restaurants using a fixed scale. Would you complain about a Beethoven symphony because you wanted Spice Girls instead?

Monarch = Beethoven.

review_info.review_text:
My friend and I came here for lunch on Saturday. I am not sure how it is at dinner, but for lunch there was no line so it was fast to get a table. The waiter was very thorough and accommodating. Both my friend and I had the blood orange margarita, which was so good because it had a jalapeño kick! But, don't worry it's not too spicy for anyone that is sensitive to spice, it was just right. 

We both ended up going with the combination plate; me the taco and enchilada and her the taco and tamale. To be honest the only reason why I didn't go with the mahi mahi taco was because it was singular (taco) versus the other tacos were plural in the name (tacos) and so I was expecting to get at least two tacos in the combo. However, only one came so I would ask that the menu be more clear. But, the food was delicious and we even had enough for leftovers. Both plates came with rice and beans too. 

There is an axxess deal for BOGO entree for lunch or dinner as well. So with all the food and drinks we had my friend and I were able to split it evenly for about $24 per person, which I think is a great deal for such a quality food.

Delicious food and drinks! Really fast service. Nice location with a nice scenic patio. They have heaters so you don't have to worry about getting cold. I ordered the burrito and my husband got the fajitas, both were delicious! I also got the margarita flight, which I highly recommend. If you're close to Amtrak on state, I would recommend stopping by!

Ate at the bar tonight for my friends birthday. The bartender Dan, (tall, light and handsome) was attentive and took great care of us! Fast drinks with a warm welcoming personality, a great guy. Good food too! my Bf and I had the tacos.. simple but tasty! Thank you!

response:
The New Black BBQ is a local business located in Santa Barbara, CA. It offers barbeque cuisine and operates as a street vendor. The business has received mixed reviews from customers. One customer had a negative experience, stating that the food truck had gone out of business without informing them after they had booked the business for their wedding. The customer had to threaten the owners with legal action to get their deposit back. This incident suggests a lack of professionalism and reliability on the part of the business.

On the other hand, another customer had a positive experience with the food. They mentioned that the sandwich they tried was tasty, although they were disappointed that one of the menu items was already sold out before the business even opened. The customer also mentioned that the menu is limited, with only three choices available.

The business does offer outdoor seating and takeout options. However, the availability of WiFi is not provided. The business has a rating of 3.5 stars, indicating that the overall customer satisfaction is average. Based on the provided information, potential customers may want to consider the mixed reviews and limited menu options before visiting The New Black BBQ.

review_info.review_text:
This food truck is out of business. I had previously booked New Black for my upcoming wedding. They skipped town without telling us, taking our $500 deposit with them. After hearing that they had gone out of business from other local food trucks, I tried contacting them several times to get my money back, but with no response. It was not until my fiancé found their personal information (their personal cell phone number and home address) and threatened to show up at their doorstep that they gave us our deposit back. 

For those of you who have them booked for an upcoming event, I would contact them immediately and try to get your deposit back as soon as possible. Sketchy!

They only have three sandwiches available and they were out of one - the Kobe brisket. They recommended the Jidori Chicken over the pork. I wonder if it was because they had more chicken than pork. Either way, it was $7 for a substantial sandwich. I would have preferred to pay $4 for a smaller portion so I could try other things. The sandwich was tasty and the chow-chow was a good complement to the chicken. It could have had a bit more acidity though.

The flavors are good, but with such a small menu, I was disappointed they were out of something before they even opened.

The food is okay.  I'm used to having my BBQ spicy.  When they asked me how I enjoyed it I told them it was okay, I was just expecting some kick to it.  Then they quipped how "If you want it spicy try some tobasco sauce, we wanted to make it good".

I have no idea what to make of that statement.  Besides that, there was not a great amount of choices.  Basically 3 choices, which are all sandwich based.

Noemi Pizza Romana is a local business located at 3534 State St in Santa Barbara, CA. It falls under the categories of Restaurants and Pizza. The restaurant has specific operating hours, which are from 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays, from 4:00 PM to 9:00 PM on Fridays, from 12:00 PM to 9:00 PM on Saturdays, and from 12:00 PM to 8:00 PM on Sundays.

According to customer reviews, Noemi Pizza Romana is highly regarded for its pizza and calzone. The toppings and pizza crust are praised for their quality, and the staff is described as super helpful. The restaurant offers ample parking and has convenient hours, making it a must-visit place.

However, there is also a negative review mentioning that the pizza, specifically the "soppressata" flavor, was disappointing. The reviewer found the crust to be bad bread with mediocre use of toppings, leading to an unsuccessful flavor combination.

Another positive review highlights the unique Roman-style pizza offered by Noemi Pizza Romana. The crust is described as incredible, and the toppings are well-balanced. Different pizza combinations, such as BBQ chicken, mushroom, and potato with goat cheese, are praised for their deliciousness.

Overall, Noemi Pizza Romana has received positive feedback for its pizza and calzone, with an average rating of 4.5 stars. It provides a comfortable outdoor seating area, offers free WiFi, accepts reservations, and provides takeout services.

review_info.review_text: By far the best pizza in town! Great toppings, amazing pizza crust and a super helpful staff, what else can you ask for? Their calzone is simply the best, you have to try it at least once! This place is a must, ample parking convenient hours. Try it and you'll be hooked.

There are two things that really bum me out: places that make bad burritos, and places that make bad pizza. Unfortunately, this was the worst "pizza" I've ever had. 
Pizza is one of those foods that should almost always give you joy, whether it's a $3 frozen pizza from the grocery store or a late night slice at a hole in the wall. 
But this pizza (and it was the "soppressata" supposedly one of the most popular) gave us no joy.

This isn't even "thick crust". This is just bad bread with mediocre use of toppings. 

Unsuccessful flavor combination.
Heavy and filling (in a bad way).

I will never make that mistake again.
I just don't understand.. if you open a pizza place, don't you have a passion for pizza? How does one mess that up so badly?

Never had Roman style pizza before and i am thoroughly impressed!!! The crust was incredible, and the ratio of toppings to bread was perfect. The toppings also matched so so well
Different pizzas we tried :
- Bbq chicken : Wow. I'm a huge fan of bbq anything, but with this specific type of dough it was even more amazing. There were some parts that were too heavy with the bbq, but overall i was blown away 
 - Mushroom : Really yummy! The umami flavor from the mushroom really came through
- Potato : Never had potato pizza before, and i will continue to get it from now on. It was so delicious, and the addition of goat cheese was heavenly. The potatoes were cooked to perfection and just *chefs kiss* 

Will definitely be back ! I want to try all the other combinations offered !

response: Taqueria La Colmena is a Mexican restaurant located at 217 Milpas St, Santa Barbara, CA. It is open every day, offering its services from 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM on weekdays and from 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM on weekends. The restaurant does not offer WiFi, outdoor seating, or reservations. Street parking is available and the restaurant is good for takeout, but it is not suitable for groups. The overall atmosphere is casual. Despite having a business rating of 4 stars, customer reviews indicate dissatisfaction in recent times. Complaints range from service issues and uncleanliness to problems with food quality and pricing. However, one customer mentioned that they still enjoy the flavor of the Adobada tacos. The restaurant has reportedly had issues with honoring promotional offers and has received criticism for perceived rudeness from staff.

review_info.review_text:
Strange experience here and won't go back. First the waitress said they couldn't make enchiladas because they had no sauce. Then we had a 2 for 1 SB axxess card and she charged $3.50 for the supposedly free item. When I asked about the charge she said " the owner told me to add tax and $2.50 more on the free item. We said we'd order elsewhere and left.  The place looked a little dirty.  After asking for an explanation a couple times about the extra $3.50 for a free item, it just didn't seem worth staying and arguing that they weren't honoring there "free " 
offer.  Figured if they just do what they want with violation of tax charges  and SB Axxess  card extra charge they might do something weird to the food. There are many other great, clean Mexican options nearby.

Bad news.

I can't say that I'll recommend this taqueria anymore.

I've been going here for years, but in the last year, something has changed. I'm not sure if it was ownership or management...or whatever. But my point is that this change is not for the better. 
The chips I had last week weren't even cooked. They were chewy and flavorless. I still do love their peanut salsa, though. But what good is peanut salsa if there's nothing to dip into it?

The service here is SO BAD now. Seriously. It's kind of shocking how bad it is. All of the women taking orders and running the register (over past year) definitely don't treat any customers with respect or kindness. They are RUDE. There is one girl who works there who I chatted with (I believe she was a high school student) and she was the ONLY one over the passed year to be even remotely friendly.

This used to be my favorite place to get an adobada taco. 
The flavor of the adobada is still my favorite in SB, but it's not worth it to be treated like a nuisance/garbage by the unenthusiastic staff.

I will continue coming here for my favorite adobada tacos until I get tired of being treated poorly. 
It really is a damn shame that this place has gone so downhill. It truly was a favorite of mine.

We came on a Sunday night around 7:30pm the waitress was extremely friendly but I am so upset with my experience. It took us 20minutes to get our food, please examine the pictures below. I got charged $9.75 for a cheese quesadilla and my friends shrimp tacos are literally just shrimp in a single tortilla. Please look at the pictures. 

To make things worse there were also bugs crawling on the walls!

Subway, located at 5146 Hollister Ave in Goleta, CA, is a fast food restaurant specializing in sandwiches. It is open every day of the week, with slightly shorter hours on Sundays. Amenities include a parking lot, take-out service, and accommodation for groups. However, it does not offer Wi-Fi, outdoor seating, or reservations. The overall ambiance is not specified. 

Customer reviews, however, are largely negative, resulting in a low average rating of 1.5 stars. Common complaints include perceived poor food quality, with meats and cheeses appearing old or crusty, and a lack of fresh vegetables. Customers also criticize the lack of cleanliness in terms of both the store and the ice machine. The staff are frequently described as unfriendly, unresponsive, and unprofessional. Consequently, many reviewers express a strong preference to avoid dining at this location in the future.

review_info.review_text: I wasn't at all impressed by this location. When I first walked in, there was nobody in sight. I noticed that all of the food (especially meat and cheese) seemed old, and crusted over on the edges like it had been sitting for a while. Then I was "greeted" by a younger lady who did not say hi and wasn't the most friendly person. There was also an older lady at the register and after I said hello, she replied "for here or to go".  Both of the employees did not seem happy and should consider selling the franchise. I didn't get a chance to look at how clean the actual store was, so I can't comment on this. I can say that I won't come back to this location under this ownership and I will instead go to the one over by Trader Joe's on Calle Real.

response: Maeda Restaurant, located at 1208 State Street in Santa Barbara, CA, is a Japanese eatery that also offers group dining. It has an overall rating of 3.5 stars based on customer reviews. Customers appreciate the good Japanese meals at a reasonable price, particularly the bento lunch combinations. However, some customers have expressed dissatisfaction with the Thai menu, comparing the Pad Thai dish to a boxed meal. There were also complaints about misunderstanding in orders, resulting in incorrect dishes being served. Some criticism was also aimed at the concept of all-you-can-eat sushi, questioning the quality of such offerings. Furthermore, the service was noted to be slow, with waitstaff seemingly disorganized. Nonetheless, the restaurant was considered affordable despite its shortcomings.

review_info.review_text: A good Japanese meal at a good price. However, I wouldn't bother with their 'Thai' menu. I could make their Pad Thai from the box at Trader Joe's. The best deal is their bento lunch combinations.

Had a craving for salmon, and was thrilled to find this place. Came in and ordered 2 orders of salmon sushi. The waiter gave me one of those faces where you're pretty sure he didn't understand, but it'd be kind of awkward to ask if he didn't understand. So he returned a while later with spicy salmon rolls. When I explained that wasn't really what I had ordered, he returned to the kitchen, then came back a minute later to explain they'd used up all the salmon on the spicy rolls. 

Fuck those guys. Two stars!

OK - let me preface this review by saying this: the term "all-you-can-eat" and sushi should NEVER EVER be in the same sentence.  The point of sushi is that it's fresh, prepared to order and any place that has "all-you-can-eat" amounts of it, is certainly not giving you anything quality.  Now I can't comment on this sushi in particular because I didn't have any (nor would I ever, anywhere) - but the Thai we had here was fine.  I had the Japanese curry which was way too soupy (not like mom's) and tasted the coconut.  Bot were so-so.  We were headed over to the Arlington Theatre to see David Byrne so were in sort of a rush but this place didn't do much to impress.  From the slow service to the waitstaff basically tripping over themselves, it was just an average experience at-best.  Cheap but not so good.

review_info.review_text:
For our girls weekend, we decided to check out Oliver's vegan restaurant. It's a quick walk from any of the rooms if you're staying at the Coast Village inn.

The outdoor patio is stunning with the most picturesque lights and gorgeous trees. Even though we were outside, the heaters kept us warm and we felt comfortable the entire time.

Hands down the best part of our meal was our cocktails. The endless summer drink was to die for.

I also highly recommend the pear and arugula flatbread, though we enjoyed everything we ate! 

I don't typically eat a lot of vegan cuisine but we loved this place and we're already planning another visit.

Oliver's is great! I've been finding myself in a couple of vegan spots lately and I'm not vegan by any stretch of the imagination. I'm one of those who will not dare consume an animal product in my coffee drinks, like could not pay me any amount of money in the world to drink cows milk - but will devour an entire block of cheese a couple hours later.

I eat what I want, when I want but my sister is Vegan and I'm totally not opposed to others living that life. I bake a bunch of vegan items and I really do love a lot of vegan options but the commitment to an entire lifestyle isn't right for me.

I'd asked my bestie if we could grab dinner at Oliver's on our way home the other night. We usually eat brekke at Jeannine's or grab coffee and pastries in Montecito on our way out to wine tasting in Los Olivos but we are never quite in need for dinner on the return because we've either already eaten a bit sooner than we hit Coast Village Rd. or I've way overdid it on McConnell's froyo stop a couple exits before here.

Either way, I knew I wanted to grab dinner so I intentionally asked the gal at McConnell's to only give me half of my froyo order because I needed to fit in dinner tonight.

My bestie is definitely not vegan so I didn't mention to him this restaurant was and as it got closer to dinner, I simply suggested this spot might be "vegetarian" I didn't want to totally scare him off of the idea.

We'd eaten a late lunch and ordered a few plates to share which was plenty!

We shared the Apple Salad, Kung Pao Cauliflower and Spinach & Artichoke Flatbread.

All three dishes were very yummy. We both really enjoyed the salad, but agreed that the Spinach & Artichoke flatbread was our fav. It was super filling and would be a great share for a larger dining party.

As much as I wanted to try dessert and under normal circumstances would have totally tried to do dessert (my froyo) before and dessert after dinner, my dessert stomach was already full and we had to table that one for our next visit.

Service was great, the salad came out quickly and the other dishes seemed to take a bit longer but it was a Sunday evening and we had no place else in the world to be so it didn't matter much.

We'll definitely return in the future. This is a great option if you are staying in the area or passing through and want a really scrumptious meal in a nice calm atmosphere.

It was a chilly night and as lovely as the patio was I wanted to cozy up in a corner booth and keep warm indoors. The patio seems perfect for warmer evenings.

Plenty of street parking out front.

Oliver's is such a cute restaurant! 
We were very pleased with the entire experience. 
The staff was amazing-  attentive and friendly. 
The outdoor ambiance is beautiful with outdoor lighting and fire pits that creates an intimate setting. There were plenty of heat lamps around to keep you warm. There is also indoor seating too! 

For dinner we had the artichoke flatbread, tomato salad, and jackfruit tacos... they were all very tasty! Oliver's is also family friendly, they had high chairs for children. They also offered pasta or cheese pizza for children to eat. 

I would definitely come back to Oliver's again. It's a great place for a nice dinner as a couple, family, or even a date night with drinks at the bar. Aesthetically, the bar was incredibly chic. I loved it. To note: parking is on the street from what I am aware, not in the actual plaza as it is saved for hotel guests there.
