response: Social Cycle is a tour business located in Santa Barbara, CA that offers tours, nightlife, event planning services, hotel & travel options, party bike rentals and more. The business is open from Monday to Sunday from 10:00 am to 10:00 pm and has an average rating of 5 stars. In terms of the customer reviews, they describe the experience as unique and fun, with a trolley-like seating arrangement where participants have to pedal their own way around. The company offers affordable prices, with good value justification for the overall experience. Social Cycle has also received positive feedback for their friendly guide and good group dining experience. However, there have been occasional complaints about organization and communication with certain locations along the route. Overall, Social Cycle seems like a great option for groups looking for a fun and memorable experience in Santa Barbara.

source_info.name: Social Cycle
source_info.categories: Tours, Bar Crawl, Nightlife, Event Planning & Services, Party Bike Rentals, Hotels & Travel

review_info.review_text:
Truly a unique experience. Had the best time. 

I've never seen anything quite like Social Cycle. It resembles a trolley with a group of people sitting inwards on a circular bar table. The above is correct, but those table-sitters are also pedaling their hearts out to fuel said trolley. 

We had used Social Cycle for a friend's birthday party. I recall the pricing per person being fairly reasonable, and well-justified for the overall experience. The cycle travels through the Funk Zone and is quite the attraction for nearby pedestrians and restaurant-goers. 

Our guide was upbeat and fun. He really made the experience an enjoyable one. Note that everyone in the party must be willing to pedal the entire time (it's really not difficult at all). We had one lady in our party who would occasionally take breaks and the cycle would noticeably slow down. Pedal, pedal, pedal!

The layout of the cycle was ideal as everyone in the party was essentially facing each other. We were able to converse and laugh together without having to turn our necks. Many memories were made that day. I'd absolutely rent this awesome cycle again.

Our group had an amazing time with social cycle and our guide Max! Pedaling was much tougher than we anticipated but we made the most of it with a group of 15. The radio on the bike was great and we were able to play our own music. There was also some storage for our personal items. 

The only downside was that it felt a little unorganized, as in the places we stopped didn't know that our large group was planning to stop there. We were also told we would get discounts at our stops but we did not receive any discounts.

Overall this is a great choice for large group events!!

Social cycle was super fun. All of the bars we went to were great recommendations. Our driver, Rob, made our trip fun and had the music blasting. 

Only complaint is, I wish we had more time on the bike! Didn't seem like we rode very far around SB and the time flew by. I'd definitely do this again with a big group!

Came here for the 1st time on a whim. Had jury duty, and did some research on places to go at.. this place was just 2 blocks down, so I decided to try it.
Ordered the chicken kabob.. delicious!!! 
Kinda hard to understand the cashier cus of his accent... 
portion is generous..left feeling full :)

I have only had a breakfast muffin sandwich.  It cost $4.99 and was loaded with scrambled egg, cheese, and your choice of meat.  I selected bacon.  I liked the sandwich and it came out quick.   The english muffin was hearty and soft, yet well toasted.  The place itself has ample seating (indoor and out) and two televisions.  I came in the early hours of the morning so it was practically empty.   The selection of candy and snacks was good.  Plenty of beverage selection, bottled, fountain, and tap drinks.
This is always our stop while traveling through. The flavors are as fun as the sandwich names. I love the different creations they have come up with. I highly recommend!

review_info.review_text:
Sad to leave this review, however have been giving the restaurant a number of visits with increasingly disappointing results.   We also have left a few messages for Dario, who never calls

1. Today we ordered a vegetable fasilli and the chicken brick dish. Neither  was very good.  The pasta dish lacked flavor. There wasn't much in terms of vegetables. It was so disappointing

I thought of taking a picture but it really was such a boring dish.  

White beans would give this some flavor and more protein. We've suggested they look at adding some beans to their  vegan vegetarian dishes but have been met with radio silence 

2 The chicken brick dish was not very good. Three people tried it and all were very disappointed. 

I'll try to add a picture of it.  Very little of it was eaten.

3. The bread is an Average plus 

We used to go here years ago and it was pretty good.  I Food today was from the Santa Barbara location on Victoria Street. We've also had disappointing meals At their montecito location.  

We really wish they would spend a little bit more time on their items and their ingredients especially for the pricing.  

Especially given they do not have good vegan options and haven't bothered to get back to us, we think we are done trying.   Ciao Ca Dario

We selected this restaurant because it had an interesting menu with vegetarian options and many positive reviews. In many ways, it offered a solid choice for our party of 10. That said, the overall impression we had was that the food was fairly ordinary. Pasta dishes were served with overcooked pasta and sauces that were unspectacular. Salads were copious, but almost entirely lettuce with lots of shredded cheese. Bread was uninspiring. Only bottled water (not tap) was offered. The one exception was a pork chop that was reportedly quite substantial and cooked exactly right. Wine choices were good, but overpriced compared to other restaurants nearby. Perhaps it was the size of our party, but our overall impression was that the restaurant isn't really trying. At the end of the meal, we had a mixup with the credit cards. Instead of splitting the bill evenly, several of us got credit card receipts for the entire party of 10! This was quickly remedied, but honestly, at this price point, we expected more.

I've been hearing about Ca' Dario for ages and planned to go last year until covid shut things down but I finally got the opportunity to go and it was delicious! The aperol spritz was yummy, the caprese salad was great! My favorite dish however was the ravioli with sage and brown butter! The flavors were amazing :-) make a reservation & try it as the restaurant is quite small.

It opens at 5 PM every day of the week, closing at 9 PM from Tuesday to Thursday and Sunday, and at 10 PM on Friday and Saturday. The restaurant offers free Wi-Fi, outdoor seating and is known for accommodating large groups. However, it does not offer takeout services. Street parking is available, with no options for a garage, validated parking, lot, or valet. The establishment has a 4-star rating. Customers have praised the quality of the food, particularly the Crispy Brussel Sprouts, Winter Beets & Marinated Burrata, and the Caramelized Cauliflower. The restaurant's service has received mixed reviews, with some customers expressing satisfaction and others citing room for improvement. Reservations are recommended due to its popularity.

review_info.review_text:
Truly a delicious "Shared Dining Experience" here in the heart of the Santa Barbara Funk Zone.

We kept hearing about the Crispy Brussel Sprouts, Winter Beets & Marinated Burrata, Caramelized Cauliflower, Cast Iron Morro Bay Black Cod, Creekstone  Prime Hanger Steak, and the Buttermilk Fried Chicken. With our large group we fortunately got to try them all . . . and each one was incredibly delicious.

Notable wine-by-the-glass which was perfect for the entire meal: Grimm's Bluff, Happy Canyon, Rose of Cabernet Sauvignon.

As cool as this special night was we were seated outside and comfortably next to one of their fireplaces, and surrounded by their portable heaters. 

Our server Laurel stuck with us from beginning to end, and she made sure the food came out promptly, and was excellent with her wine and cocktails recommendations. Can't say enough how thorough she was in making sure our night was special. Also special thanks to host Alberto for keeping an eye on us throughout the evening. 

Highly recommend making reservations to this very special restaurant as it is truly a hot-spot in Santa Barbara. Afterwards Alberto walked us next door to Pearl Social for a continued evening of specialty cocktails.

The food was good to great, where the experience fell apart was in the service.    The restaurant was mostly empty when we arrived yet (during covid)  we were seated right next two other tables.   I assumed the other tables had reservations but remained empty for the remainder of our stay.   The staff was oblivious to the tables they did have, forgetting to recover tables when food was served, ignoring customers waving checks ready to leave, adding plates to our table without removing empty dishes.  Everyone was on autopilot.   It was a real shame because the food was beautiful and delicious.   I would not return despite that.

My partner and I celebrated our anniversary the other night here. It was our first time and our waiter Oscar was friendly and treated us so well! 

Experience: 5/5
We were welcomed with a little anniversary card which was very thoughtful.  The outdoor seating area was really nice and there were heat lamps to keep us warm. The food came out in a timely manner and when we were done with everything, Oscar brought out some complimentary pours of rose to celebrate our special night. Thanks Oscar, you're awesome!!

Food: 4/5
We were brought some popcorn to snack on before the meal. Not sure what the seasoning is but it's really good! The mushroom tartine we ordered was also great and probably my favorite item of the night. Brussel sprouts were delicious too but the sauce was a little heavy for me. Lastly, the famous boneless fried chicken was tasty but not the best fried chicken I've ever had. Maybe I just prefer bones-in. I enjoyed the various dipping sauces on the plate as well.

Drinks: 5/5
My partner had the black Manhattan and I had the gimlet and both were very good, no complaints.

Definitely want to come back to try everything else on the menu!

review_info.review_text: THE FRENCH TABLE is no longer in business but there is a new restaurant in it's place called PIANO GASTROLOUNGE.  Great food, great service and the same incredible view. It was delicious.  I think it was the carmelized onions that did the trick and made it so unique.  Sit ouside if you can, it is so quiet, beautiful and relaxing.

This place totally came out of nowhere and it is adorable! 

My server named Dustin was incredibly attentive and kind. 

Plus this world needs more creperies, and The French Table excels in that arena.

It's sad to saw but the food was really good but the service was horrid. Working in the food industry I was shocked. My friend and I were ignored by the first waiter who was flirting with a group of girls so we went to the bar. The bartender was busy talking with off the clock staff drinking for free. We were basically ignored. She also made up an excuse not to use our living social deal. Won't be going back. Staff was a joke.

Pueblo Pollo is a local restaurant located at 2984 State St in Santa Barbara, CA. The restaurant specializes in New Mexican cuisine and Mexican fast food. According to the provided structured data, Pueblo Pollo offers free WiFi and outdoor seating. They also provide takeout services and have parking available on the street and in a nearby lot.

The restaurant's operating hours are as follows: Tuesday to Sunday from 10:0 am to 10:0 pm, with the exception of Friday when they close at 5:0 pm. It is closed on Mondays.

Based on customer reviews, Pueblo Pollo has received mixed feedback. One customer mentioned that the food did not meet their expectations, with lukewarm sides and chicken that seemed off in taste and appearance. They speculated that the lack of freshness could be due to the restaurant not being busy enough. Another customer, however, praised the chicken and rice, mentioning that they were nicely done and tasty. They did mention that the portion size of the rice was small.

Overall, Pueblo Pollo has a rating of 2.5 stars. While some customers had negative experiences with the food, others enjoyed the taste. It may be worth visiting Pueblo Pollo for those who are looking for New Mexican cuisine or Mexican fast food in Santa Barbara.

review_info.review_text:
if you want your moneys worth or any type of decent food that you pay for this isnt the place for it , go elsewhere.
lukewarm sides, chicken seems a bit off , taste & lookswise.

my guess is they arent busy enough to keep things going fresh and hot here constantly , at the end you end up with not fresh food or even past due food.

just dont , trust me..

Really nicely done chicken not overcooked or dry and the rice was tasty too! Going to go back but honestly want to ask for larger portions on the rice. Felt like it was small even for a child.  But great tasting food and chicken. 7.99$ for 2 piece meal same as el pollo loco

Went here to see if the food was any better now that it's not an El Pollo loco. The bar was set low and I had hoped that they could have served me some decent chicken, but, alas, they could not. Chicken was greasy but not in a good way. The beans and rice had the texture and taste as if they had been laying out for most of the day. Needless to say, I wasn't impressed with food. I'm not surprised considering the photos on google look like stock photos, pretty lame. Do yourself a favor and go down to El Mercado plaza near the 154 and hit up El Rincon or Palapa(next to the adult store and methadone clinic) both of those places will give you a meal worthy of your hard earned money. This place has decided to continue in the mediocre footsteps of El Pollo Loco and have, somehow, taken the food down  another step. Perhaps they are competing for the worst food in town award? PASS.

response: The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf is a food, coffee, and tea restaurant located at 3052 De La Vina, Santa Barbara, CA. The restaurant operates between 6:00 am and 6:00 pm all week, offers free Wi-Fi, outdoor seating, and take-out services. While there is no garage, street, validated, or valet parking, a parking lot is available. Despite a decent business rating of 3.5 stars, customer reviews highlight issues with staff rudeness and lack of care for customers. Some customers have complained about their drink orders being withheld and being treated with disrespect. Others have appreciated the shaded location, available parking, power outlets, and the overall affordability of the restaurant. However, they also noted that some staff members were unkind and made them feel like a burden.

review_info.review_text: My gripe with my experience would pertain to the rudeness of the wait staff and the lack of care towards their customer. I find it absurd that that they have the audacity to charge for a cup after their cup failed to preform. Please fulfill your coffee needs elsewhere.

Well, if you're in a hurry and, say, order ahead of time like I do, leave extra time for a lecture from the staff if they don't like the way you ordered your drink. My drink was withheld. I was held up in the morning by an employee. She wasn't friendly or accommodating. It wasn't as if I was patronizing their business. I was essentially scolded with no respect for my time or the fact that I purchase things here often. This isn't the first time. We were treated rudely about refills on more than one occasion with the staff demanding a receipt (even when they never gave us one). I don't need the third degree or rude treatment when I'm overpaying for coffee on a Monday morning. I suggest going to the State Street location where the staff is always friendly, accommodating, and wonderful.

Nice shaded location (near TJ's) and there is almost always a parking space. One of the few coffee shops around town that has power outlets. Solid coffee. Decent Jasmine and Dragonwell green tea. $1.00 refill for coffee. The service is great for the most part - it seems like quite a few people work here. However, the employee this morning left a bad taste in my mouth. She didn't say anything specifically unkind, but I got the feeling my presence was a burden to her. Maybe she is in pain and doesn't have much kindness to give. I've worked many years in retail - and I know workers aren't robots and have complex inner lives - but even at my worst I could fake it, or at least not be a grouch to my customers. I left feeling a bit resentful (or hurt) that a stranger would be so rigid and unkind to me. I don't deserve that! I'll get over it though haha. For prospective customers: the organic light roast (Peru) was infinitely better than the dark roast, which I had for refill. Four stars because of the location, affordability, power outlets, and most of the customer service. I couldn't go full 5 stars because, frankly, it's 2020 and you can find tastier, more complex, higher-quality coffee elsewhere.

1. Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C).
2. Cut sweet potatoes into 1/2-inch sticks or wedges.

7. Let the wedges cool for 5 minutes before serving.

6. Once the grill is heated, leave the porterhouse steak out at room temperature for about an hour before cooking.

response: AF-C, or AF 'continuous', is designed for tracking moving subjects. The camera continuously focuses on the subject as it moves, keeping it in focus whether it's moving towards or away from the camera, or laterally. On the other hand, AF-A, or AF 'auto', automatically switches between single and continuous modes depending on the subject's movement. This mode requires less effort from the photographer but relies on the camera's ability to correctly guess the subject of focus, which may lead to unexpected results.

response:
To sew a zipper gusset, follow these steps:

1. Divide the number of gussets needed in half, which means 2 gussets for each side seam.
2. Measure out and mark two points on the left side of the dress and two points on the right side, leaving room for the zipper.
3. Trace the pattern onto the remaining fabric and cut out the pieces.
4. Sew a zipper sandwich by placing a piece of lining fabric face up, followed by the zipper and then the outer fabric, right side facing down. Align the three edges and sew across the top between the edge of the zipper sandwich and the zipper teeth (closer to the zipper feet).
5. Repeat this step for the other side of the zipper.
6. Pin the zipper gusset to the zipper with the right sides facing each other, leaving about 1/4" space from the center.
7. Use a zipper foot to sew a line near the seam line to secure the position.
8. Flip the lining to the bottom of the main zipper gusset and stitch on the seam line.
9. Repeat sewing the other side of the zipper gusset.
10. The width of the zipper between the gussets should measure 1/2".
11. Switch back to a normal foot and stitch on the seam allowance around the zipper gusset so that the main and lining fabric attach together neatly.
12. Stitch lightly on the piping seam allowance at the curve.
13. Place the zipper gusset on the pencil case body with the ends aligned to the center markings.
14. Sew from the marking to the marking at both ends.
15. Add any additional decorative elements such as buttons or elastic.

passage 1:Directions. Prep. Cook. Ready In. 1  Place eggs into a saucepan and pour in cold water to cover; place over high heat. 2  When the water just starts to simmer, turn off heat, cover pan with a lid, and let stand for 17 minutes. 3  Don't peek. 4  Pour out the hot water and pour cold water over eggs.

passage 2:1 If you're not particular about how pretty your peeled eggs are, you can skip the refrigerator and start peeling them right after chilling them. 2  To test whether an egg is hard-boiled without breaking it, whirl it on a table. 3  If it spins fast and easy, it is hard boiled. 4  If it wobbles, it needs more time.

passage 3:There are two main problems when it comes to hard-boiled eggs: green-gray yolks and shells that just won’t peel off. Make hard-boiled eggs headache-free by following this easy method. First, place the cold eggs in a single layer in a pan with enough cold water to cover them by about 1 inch. Then, place the pan on the stove over high heat. Shutterstock. As soon as the water comes to a boil turn the heat off, cover the pan, and remove it from the heat. Allow the eggs to sit in the water until they are cooked; about 9 minutes for a medium egg, 12 minutes for a large egg, and 15 minutes for an extra-large egg.

To attach multiple picture frames together, you can use a couple of methods. One way is to use a stand grouping method where you select two or three frames of the same wood molding. Attach two small hinges to the connecting sides of the frames.

You can always unscrew them at a later date to change the picture if you want. Attach a hanging wire to the back, hang it up and step back to enjoy the results. 

If you're hanging multiple pictures together, it may be helpful to test ideas by laying the group of pictures out on the floor first.

1. Each player takes turns rolling the six dice.
2. If no point dice appear (i.e., if none of the dice show a 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6), a Farkle occurs and the player loses all the point dice they have collected during that turn.

4. Points are recorded on a scratch paper, but only if the player chooses to stop rolling without a Farkle.
5. The objective of the game is to have the highest score after 10 rounds of play.

response: To make a hot water heater circulate, a hot water circulation pump is needed. This pump sends cool water in the pipes back to the water heater through a return line. The pump circulates this water through the water heater as needed to keep it hot, ensuring hot water is always available. Alternatively, recirculating pumps can be used to rapidly pull hot water from a water heater, while simultaneously sending cool water from the hot water lines back to the water heater to be reheated and reused. These systems can be controlled by the push of a button, a timer, or a motion sensor. However, it should be noted that heat loss from the pipes can occur, requiring the water heater to use more fuel.

response:
To cook a smoked pork picnic shoulder in the oven, follow these steps:

1. Preheat your oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
2. Place the pork shoulder on a rack in a shallow roasting pan. This will allow excess fat to drain away during cooking.
3. Insert an oven-proof meat thermometer into a meaty section of the shoulder roast. Make sure to avoid placing it near a bone.
4. Cover the roasting pan loosely with aluminum foil.
5. Roast the pork shoulder in the preheated oven for approximately 2-3 hours, or until the internal temperature reaches 195-205 degrees Fahrenheit when measured with a meat thermometer.
6. Remove the aluminum foil after about 2 hours and continue roasting until the skin is crispy and golden brown.
7. Let the pork shoulder rest for at least 10-15 minutes before slicing and serving.

source_info.question: what is the effect of carbon footprint
source_info.passages:
passage 1:Your carbon footprint measures the environmental impact of your lifestyle. Everything you do has an impact --- positive or negative --- on the environment. That's the concept behind your carbon footprint, which is one method of measuring the environmental effect of your lifestyle. A carbon footprint, measured in tons, indicates the amount of carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases that are produced as a result of your daily activities. You can reduce your footprint by changing the way you live your life. Even seemingly tiny changes can make a significant difference.

passage 2:It all comes back to the average carbon footprint. The average per capita carbon footprint is 6 tons per year. In the U.S. the average is 20 tons per year, and a third of that is created by automobile emissions -- meaning your car itself can put out over 6 tons of C02 a year -- enough for two people.

passage 3:So what exactly is a carbon footprint? In simplest terms, carbon footprint is the total amount of greenhouse gases produced by various human activities within a given time frame. Carbon footprint is usually measured in tons of carbon dioxide (CO2) released into the atmosphere. Your home has a carbon footprint if you use oil, coal or gas to heat it. That cheeseburger at your favorite restaurant has a carbon footprint: raising the beef and wheat and operating the restaurant all involves greenhouse gases. Your car has a carbon footprint, dependent on the vehicle’s fuel consumption and driving distance.

1. Preheat a gas or charcoal grill to medium temperature (350°F to 450°F).
2. Remove the ribs from their foil wrap, and place them meaty-side up on the grill. Brush the ribs with some sauce and cover the grill. Cook for 5 minutes, then flip and brush again before cooking for an additional 5 minutes. Continue this process until the sauce has thickened and the ribs have grill marks. The total grilling time will be 20 minutes.
3. If you prefer to cook the ribs in an oven, remove the membrane from the bottom of the ribs using a knife. Start at the narrow end and pull off the membrane in one piece. Place the ribs in a resealable bag and add enough BBQ sauce to cover them. Line a baking pan with heavy-duty foil, making sure there is plenty of overlapping foil to create a tent around the ribs. Bake in the preheated oven at 275°F for 2 hours. After 2 hours, increase the temperature to 375°F and bake for an additional 15 minutes.

response:
Based on the provided passages, the main difference between ad hominem fallacy and poisoning the well fallacy is the timing of the attack.

Ad hominem fallacy occurs when an attack is made on a person's character, motive, or other attribute directly related to their argument, rather than attacking the argument itself. This type of attack can happen at any point during a debate or discussion.

On the other hand, poisoning the well fallacy involves making an ad hominem attack (i.e., attacking a person's character or integrity) before the merits of a case can be considered. In other words, it is an attempt to discredit a person's argument by attacking their personal integrity or intelligence before the discussion has even begun.

So, while both fallacies involve attacking a person's character rather than their argument, ad hominem fallacy happens after the argument has been presented, while poisoning the well fallacy happens before the argument is even presented.

* Is not registered with the government
* Does not give the owner exclusive rights to use the mark nationwide

* Can only be protected under common law, which may not provide sufficient legal remedies in cases of infringement.

To make panko crumbs, you can follow these steps:

1. Preheat an oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
2. Torn pieces of bread or chunks of white bread can be pushed through the shredding disk of a food processor to make coarse crumbs.
3. Spread the crumbs on a baking sheet.
4. Bake in preheated oven until crumbs are dry but not toasted, 6 to 8 minutes. Be careful not to let the crumbs brown too much.
5. Shake the sheet twice during baking to evenly dry crumbs.
6. Remove from the oven and let the crumbs cool completely.
7. Once cooled, transfer the crumbs to an airtight container and store at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.

response: Tobiano and overo are two basic patterns found in paint horses. Tobiano is characterized by a large patch of clearly lined color on a white coat, with the white color crossing the topline between the wither and the tail. Tobianos generally have a dark colored face, stockings or socks, and often have dual colored tails. On the other hand, Overos can also have stockings or socks if they carry the sabino gene. It is a misconception that if the white markings cross the back, it is a tobiano and if not, it's an overo, as many minimally marked tobianos do not have white that crosses the back, and many overos do.

response:
To clean tarnished jewelry at home, you can follow these steps:

For items that are merely dull, filmy or starting to discolor, mix a few drops of mild dish soap with warm water and dip in a soft cloth. Rub the jewelry, then rinse in cool water and buff with a cloth until dry.

For heavier tarnish, mix a paste of three parts baking soda to one part water. Wet the silver and apply the cleaner with a soft, lint-free cloth (not paper towels, which can scratch).

To clean a diamond, use warm soapy water and a soft-bristle brush or old toothbrush. Rinse in cool water and pat dry with a soft cloth.

If your silver is lightly tarnished, a salt bath should take the tarnish right off. Pour two cups of hot water into a bowl, cover the jewelry with the water, and let it sit for an hour. For just one piece of jewelry, use less water. If you're cleaning a lot of jewelry at once, you can use more water. For gemstone jewelry, make sure that the stones won't be affected by being submerged in a saltwater solution.

Global egalitarianism refers to a concept of global justice that emphasizes the importance of equality among individuals and groups worldwide. According to this perspective, global justice requires that all individuals have equal access to resources and opportunities, regardless of their cultural background or location.

The first passage highlights the limitations of global egalitarianism by arguing that measuring the resources or opportunities available to people in different societies in a way that is neutral as between cultures is impossible. Therefore, the principle of global justice cannot be based solely on equality of resources or equality of opportunity.

The second passage notes that the world is highly unequal in socio-economic terms, with certain individuals and groups having more wealth and opportunities than others. This inequality is seen as a major challenge to global justice.

The third passage distinguishes between instrumental and non-instrumental forms of egalitarianism. Instrumental egalitarianism seeks to promote equality as a means to achieve some other goal, while non-instrumental egalitarianism values equality for its own sake or as partially constituting some other end.

Therefore, based on the given passages, global egalitarianism can be understood as a conception of global justice that prioritizes equality among individuals and groups worldwide, but recognizes the challenges involved in measuring and achieving equality in a global context.

1. Preheat the oven to 400 degrees.
2. Rinse and dry the hens.
3. Place parsley, rosemary, thyme, garlic, lemon, salt, and pepper in a food processor and blend until finely chopped. With the machine running, add olive oil.
4. Loosen the skin of the hens and put 1 tablespoon of the herb mixture under the skin of each hen, smoothing it to cover the breasts.
5. Place the hens on a large rimmed baking sheet, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate overnight.
6. Remove the hens from the refrigerator and bring them to room temperature (about 1 hour).
7. Roast the hens breast side down for 25 minutes, then flip and roast for an additional 25-35 minutes, or until they are cooked through.
8. Remove the hens from the oven and let them rest for at least 10 minutes before serving.
